## **Why do we need an agent ?**

It is not as simple as using OpenAI APIs (or any other provider) to create a chat agent capable of engaging with your product’s users and providing replies tailored to your domain.

In this post, we will discuss why you should use an agent or create your own if you want to give a personalized and relevant experience to your users.

Let’s start with some Incorta samples. The first example on top is when answered directly by the LLM model, while the second example is the result of dealing with LLM model via [OpenCopilot](https://github.com/Incorta/OpenCopilot) (Incorta’s concept chat agent):

As you can see, the distinction is in context and business domain awareness. In general, the custom agent is far better capable of providing well-crafted and appropriate responses. Answers that consider the business domain of your product, as well as the user’s background and personal history.

## Types of Chat Agents:

Generally speaking, two types of chat agents, do exist:

- **One-shot:** In this case the agent will decide upon a single action, based on user’s question, and go to execute that action. Usually this is very limited in capacity and functionality
- **Plan-and-execute:** More advanced agents, that break the problem first into sub-tasks, and then go about executing them one by one. Potentially chaining the responses till a final answer is obtained

## Elements of General Plan-and-Exec Chat Agent

We will explore the key elements that make up the majority of bespoke Chat Agents.

1. **Indexed Knowledge Base:** This is a standout feature that distinguishes the traditional zero-shot chat messaging from a more advanced custom agent. In the zero-shot approach, questions are simply forwarded to a GPT API and the response is awaited. However, this method may not always be efficient as the GPT system may lack up-to-date knowledge about your product documentation, API capabilities, and customer history. Some of this information may not even be publicly accessible. In other words, an indexed knowledge base brings a higher level of customization and specificity to your chat agent.
2. **Task Planning:** This is usually the initial phase where the user’s question, accompanied by a planning prompt, is forwarded to a language model for chat. The formulated plan is then received and stored for subsequent execution.
3. **Task Execution:** The agent then searches the previously defined task list and attempts to perform them using a supported execution engine. The stages involved in task execution are often well-defined and tailored to the needs of the organization. Public service providers, such as search engines, may be used on occasion.
4. **Result Evaluation/ ReAct:** This is an intriguing aspect of the process. Here, the agent evaluates the outcome, determines its adequacy, and decides whether further investigation or summarization is required. In some instances, the agent may have to revisit the planning phase to respond appropriately to the obtained results.
5. **Memory:** An effective agent will generally require some form of short-term or long-term memory. This is important for handling future inquiries and maintaining the continuity of conversations.

## Popular Agents:

- **AutoGPT:** Works on the question continuously, consulting search engines (and other plugins) to conduct actions. It will continue to work autonomously until a response is obtained.. [https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT)

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*ZL7EYV42NEDbntr9R6mhUw.png)

AutoGPT High Level general flow

- **BabyAGI:** Has superior reasoning and long-term analysis for determining which task should be completed next. Although AutoGPT appears to do better with open-ended queries. BabyAGI is better designed for activities that involve more thinking and task decomposition. It can do so because it maintains a list of all tasks and prioritizes which task should be completed next.

[https://github.com/yoheinakajima/babyagi](https://github.com/yoheinakajima/babyagi)

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:651/1*xJPyx8eJBtM8gBsfgp8UqA.png)

BabyAGI general flow

- **LangChain Agent:** While LangChain is primarily constructed from modular components, it also includes several agents for specific tasks. One notable agent is the plan-and-execute agent, which mitigates some limitations related to unbounded execution found in the other agents. This agent operates by first formulating a plan, then sequentially processing each stage using a sub-loop. The sub-loop consists of execution, evaluation, another round (or more) of evaluation/execution, and finally completion of the single-step. And so-on till all steps are done.

## Use vs. Build, when should you build your own ?

In broad terms, it’s often more efficient to utilize existing resources rather than investing substantial funds to start from zero and create something completely new. However, it’s important to note that general agents don’t usually fit all sizes. There could be several reasons why you may not find a perfect fit, and these reasons can differ widely.

But before we delve deeper, let’s consider the typical disadvantages associated with general agents. Allow me to share our insights based on the experiments and observations we’ve conducted:

- **Expense:** General agents such as BabyAGI and Auto-GPT can be quite expensive. This is because they can enter loops and consume a large number of API tokens from OpenAI (or any other provider), which directly corresponds to monetary costs.
- **Simplicity:** At times, the task you want to accomplish may be simple or have a predictable structure. In such cases, using general agents might be excessively complex and unnecessary.
- **Innovation:** The quest for improved designs is an infinite journey, and superior designs will always surface. However, this can often be a pitfall, as you may believe you’ve developed a new design when in reality, it’s not unique. To avoid this trap, especially if you’re new to the field and think you’re crafting something novel, it’s always wise to first consult the community about your concept.

Regarding the downsides, as is often the case with any well-liked open-source system, such as AutoGPT, it attracts substantial community interest and a vast base of contributors. Therefore, if it aligns with your use case, you would benefit from the strength and dynamism of an engaged community offering extensive support.

## Why did we chose to build a new Agent ?

In the context of Incorta, we have a very specific and limited application. The primary task is answering an analytics-related query. This typically involves a series of well-defined steps:

- Comprehending the question
- Gathering pertinent metadata
- Executing a query, and providing a response.

Given the narrow focus of our mission, solutions such as BabyAGI and AutoGPT, seem unnecessarily complex. Their tendency to involve a broad, potentially limitless task loop does not align well with our goal of addressing distinct and well-structured problems.

Therefore, we aim to optimize our approach for several key attributes:

- Minimal planning costs
- Predictable and pre-determined execution path
- Assured task completion.

## OpenCopilot Design:

We suggest the following system design for applications with similar requirements to ours, as an alternative to the conventional endless task execution loops. Our design involves a three-tiered approach:

1. **High-Level Plan:** This tier involves providing the agent with essential instructions. In layman’s terms, we introduce to GPT what Incorta can do, and then request GPT to produce a high-level plan.
2. **Low-Level Plan:** Here, the high-level tasks are broken down, indicating which operator can perform each task. Subsequently, the Low-Level planning stage converts the operator’s high-level task into a granular, low-level task.
3. **Command Extraction:** Each low-level task is then relayed to GPT, accompanied by guidelines on how to transform it into a well-formulated command that the operator can execute.

This tiered architecture significantly cuts down costs. Each stage allows us to feed GPT a highly specific prompt containing just enough information to plan at that particular level. This avoids the potential confusion that could arise from inundating GPT with all the information at once.

Although BabyAGI can deliver similar results, it runs the risk of entering endless loops. Our tiered approach provides a predictable and assured path to a solution.

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*k8a7YPSqr1Ull6m-yCyaJQ.png)

High level system overview and main components

Take note of the “Operators” box in the diagram. Operators, represent the low-level processors in our system. Here are some examples of operators we used for [OpenCopilot](https://github.com/Incorta/OpenCopilot):

1. **QueryWriterOperator:** This operator can convert natural language processing (NLP) text into an SQL statement.
2. **QueryRunnerOperator:** This operator is capable of executing queries and retrieving results from Incorta.
3. **SchemaOperator:** This operator can extract the metadata and column names from the schema that are relevant to the question being asked.
4. **UITextOperator:** This operator can generate general text responses to the user.
5. **UIChartOperator:** This operator is capable of creating Javascript charts using various dialects.

## What’s next for Incorta’s OpenCopilot

Check OpenCopilot’s Github: [https://github.com/Incorta/OpenCopilot](https://github.com/Incorta/OpenCopilot)

## Where to go next

If you are new to the field of GPT Agents, it would be helpful to begin by examining these two open-source options:

1. AutoGPT: [AutoGPT GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT)
2. BabyAGI: [BabyAGI GitHub Repository](https://github.com/yoheinakajima/babyagi)

Following this, you should investigate whether there are other open-source alternatives that align with your particular use case.

If you remain set on building your own system, then familiarizing yourself with the following concepts and tools is highly recommended:

1. **Prompt Engineering:** This is a fundamental skill for interacting with conversational large language models (LLMs).
2. **LangChain:** This tool contains a variety of components that could significantly streamline the process of constructing your own agent.
3. **Vector/Embedding Databases:** Examples include Pinecone and ChromaDB. These databases are where you would be storing your data and searching for your short/ long term memory.
